current.text: He is a projected starter with CJ McCollum, Nickeil Alexander-Walker, Dyson Daniels and Onyeka Okongwu. Each starter should play 30-plus minutes.
Atlanta has no true point guard. McCollum, Alexander-Walker, Johnson and Daniels share the ball handling.

McCollum is on the roster for the full season. In the part of last season he played with McCollum, Johnson's assists fell by about one per game. His time on ball, steals, blocks and shooting also dropped, and he was not a top 30 player.
His steals, blocks and shooting efficiency dropped late last season, after a big jump in minutes. His shooting also dropped in the playoffs.
Experts expect sharing the ball with McCollum to cut his assists, usage, steals and shooting a little. They think last season's numbers and first-round value will be hard to keep.
Experts do not see him as a first-round pick in category leagues. Lloyd would take him in the middle of round two. Others call him a bust at pick 11 and too high at picks 9 or 10.
He went for 33 USD in an expert auction mock draft.
Atlanta plays 4-4-3 games in our playoff weeks (March 28 end). The team has 14 back-to-backs, but experts do not expect it to rest players, and it did not shut players down last season.

durable.text: He is a strong playmaker and rebounder for a forward. His rebounds and assists are league outliers, and his assists are far above other forwards. He also scores a lot.
He commits many turnovers. This is his clear weak category.
Experts call his percentages and three-point shooting iffy.
He was injured in every season before 2025-26, which was his first healthy season. His past injuries include wrist and shoulder injuries.
Experts disagree on his injury risk. Lloyd calls the past injuries fluky and is not concerned. Others say he has a checkered medical history and that one healthy season does not make him reliable.
Experts rate him clearly higher in points leagues than in category leagues.

note: Yahoo (46 USD, rank 12) and ESPN (56 USD, rank 9) both price him as a first-rounder. Experts see him as a mid second-rounder in 9-cat, and he went for 34 USD in our league last season and 33 USD in an expert mock, so 35 to 40 USD looks like a fair ceiling for us. He fits a punt TO build best, where his elite rebounds and assists from a forward slot count fully. Early in the season, check whether his assists, steals and FG% hold up with McCollum on the floor.
